title: Choose the smallest reasoning contract that can justify the answer
description: Route a decision to rules, causal inference, or rapid adaptation. The output shows whether the engine and evidence can support the claim being requested.

modes.label: Symbolic rules
modes.detail: Derive a conclusion from explicit facts, constraints, and precedence rules.
modes.blindSpot: Rules do not estimate an intervention or learn a new task distribution.

modes.label: Causal model
modes.detail: Estimate what changes when the system intervenes rather than merely observes.
modes.blindSpot: The answer depends on graph and identification assumptions.

modes.label: Fast adaptation
modes.detail: Use prior tasks to adapt a model to a related task from a small support set.
modes.blindSpot: Adaptation can fail when the new task is outside the meta-training distribution.

evidencePolicies.label: Verified decision evidence
evidencePolicies.detail: Versioned facts, rules, assumptions, and provenance are available.

evidencePolicies.label: Observational history only
evidencePolicies.detail: Past behavior is available, but intervention assumptions are not documented.

evidencePolicies.label: Reviewed support examples
evidencePolicies.detail: A small labeled set represents the new task and its acceptance boundary.

scenarios.label: Explain an eligibility decision
scenarios.detail: A reviewer must see which policy clauses and applicant facts imply approval or denial.
scenarios.question: Does this applicant satisfy every mandatory policy condition?
scenarios.claim: A deductive decision with a reproducible proof trace
scenarios.failure: A statistical score cannot show that every mandatory rule was satisfied.

scenarios.label: Predict a retention-policy intervention
scenarios.detail: The team needs the effect of extending a grace period, not another correlation report.
scenarios.question: What would retention be if the grace period changed from 7 to 14 days?
scenarios.claim: An intervention estimate with explicit identification assumptions
scenarios.failure: Observed association may be explained by account maturity or selection.

scenarios.label: Adapt intent detection to a new market
scenarios.detail: Only a small reviewed support set exists, but related markets provide prior tasks.
scenarios.question: Can the classifier adapt without a full new-market training cycle?
scenarios.claim: A measured few-shot adaptation result on a protected query set
scenarios.failure: A generic pretrained model can appear fluent while missing local intent boundaries.
